Messages.Author: BogusMagus
Messages.Body:
(I wasn't sure if I should make a new thread.)

I made the list for myself, but maybe someone else will find it useful?

Sorry if I have made any mistake.

*** Heirs to the Blood Expansion (2010) ***

Booster Packs (Random)

* 168 cards (Rare 54, Vampire 58, Common 56)
Crypt 58
Library 110

* All new.

*** Heirs to the Blood Reprint Bundles (2018) ***

2 Bundles (Fixed)

* All reprint, no new card.

* 2 Bundles together
Crypt 58
Library 76

* Cards that were NOT reprinted
Crypt 0
Library 34

Barrenness
Bliss

Striga
Strix
Summon History
Threading the Path of Orpheus
Three's a Crowd
Treat the Sick Mind
Unleash Hell's Fury
Warding the Beast

So,

NO "not a Discipline" (Maleficia, Striga) cards. 12 in total?

NO Summon History, NO Unleash Hell's Fury.
Because they are in Anthology?

* The cards that I think should have made it or wish it did.

Three's a Crowd. I think this card is important for Blood Brothers (combat) decks.
I personally have enough, though.

Hatch the Viper. I personally want more.
(Since it was rare, I think I only have two. I have never used it.)
But since it has nothing to do with Bloodline clans, I think it is reasonable that it was dropped.

Here goes some feedback:

As occurs with Books, Card Games too are totally free of importing fees by law here in Brazil.
Board Games is begining to have a similar treatment too...

But as pointed by Fernando Cesar (a.k.a.  Sydnelson - Prince of Rio de Janeiro), Márcio Pinheiro (a.k.a.  fmcpce - Brazilian National Coordinator) and some others in various threads on facebook: The players of VTES is paying a huge amount of importing fees, becouse poorly descriptions on the postal manifests.

Drivethrucards is declaring the content only as "Printed Material". The correct must be to declare "Colectible Card Game".
There is even players that says to have contacted DriveThru regarding that situation, asking for a correct description on the packages. But no answer was given.

May be White Wolf, VEKN and Black Chantry can contact DriveThru regarding improving that aspect of international shipments.

Regarding other countries
Don't know if other countries have similar legislation or rules regarding importing books and card games. So, would be great to know, if someone can tell.

Priest of Rio de Janeiro

My blog:  Portal Distant Kingdoms
Facebook:  Distant Kingdoms
Youtube:  Distant Shore

Messages.Author: Snodig
Messages.Body: There are similar regulations in parts of Europe, but card games usually fall under “printed material”, and is taxed as books, so it makes little difference as far as I know.
